title: GWTC-4.0: Tests of General Relativity. II. Parameterized Tests
extended_summary:
This paper is part of the GWTC-4.0 series on tests of general relativity using gravitational-wave observations from compact binary coalescence events. It focuses on parameterized tests of general relativity and related propagation effects, asking whether observed gravitational-wave signals show evidence for deviations from the GR waveform predictions.

The study does not examine educational interventions or human participants in an education setting. Instead, it analyzes gravitational-wave event data from the LIGO–Virgo–KAGRA detectors, applying multiple testing frameworks, including FTI and TIGER, to constrain deviations in inspiral post-Newtonian coefficients, post-inspiral coefficients, spin-induced multipole terms, line-of-sight acceleration, and propagation effects such as modified dispersion and spacetime-symmetry breaking.

The analyzed events come from observing runs O1 through O4a, with results reported for selected confident signals that met analysis criteria. The paper finds no compelling evidence for departures from GR overall, reports improved bounds on several deviation parameters, and updates the bound on the graviton mass. Because this is a physics methods/results paper with no K-12 or education-related study, it is not relevant to the requested education evidence base.
